SECTION 7 — CAVEMAN SUMMARY

Big idea: each side promise cover other side when outsider sue. Then cap on how much either side owe.

7.1 — Both sides cover each other
If outsider sue you because of other side's mess, other side pay. Other side pay lawyer, pay settlement, pay fine. Covers you, your bosses, your workers.

Other side must cover when:
(a) they break promise in contract
(b) they very careless or do harm on purpose
(c) their work product get accused of stealing someone else's IP

But (c) not apply if:
- you changed their work
- you mixed their work with other stuff, and mix caused problem
- you used work in way contract not allow

7.2 — How to claim cover
When sued:
1. Tell other side fast, in writing. Tell late? Still covered, unless late hurt their case.
2. Let other side run defense and settle. But they cannot settle in way that says you guilty or makes you do things (not just pay money) without your OK. You not say no without good reason.
3. Help them. They pay cost of help.

7.3 — Cap on blame money
Two rules:

Rule one: no side pay other for indirect harm. No lost profit. No lost revenue. No lost reputation. No lost data. Even if warned harm might happen.

Rule two: total money one side owe other, whole contract, capped at bigger of:
(A) fees customer paid or owe provider in 12 months before first bad event, or
(B) $100,000.

Caps not apply for four things:
- 7.1 cover duty
- breaking secrecy (Section 9)
- very careless or on-purpose harm
- stealing other side's IP

So those four? No cap. Full blame money.

KEY WORDS, PLAIN

Indemnify: "I pay if you get sued for my mess." Insurance-like promise.

Hold harmless: "I will not let this hurt you." Goes with indemnify.

Defend: pay for and run lawyers in court fight.

Indemnifying Party: side doing paying.

Indemnified Parties: side getting protected, plus their bosses, workers, agents.

Third-party claim: outsider sue. Not you vs. me. Someone else vs. one of us.

Claims: lawsuits, demands, legal actions from outsider.

Losses: all cost that come from Claim. Money paid, fines, lawyer bills.

Representation / warranty / covenant: promise in contract. Rep = "this is true." Warranty = "I guarantee this." Covenant = "I will do this."

Gross negligence: very very careless. Way past normal mistake.

Willful misconduct: did bad thing on purpose.

Deliverables: work product one side hand over.

Intellectual property (IP): ideas someone own. Patents, copyright, trademarks, secrets.

Infringe / misappropriate: infringe = use someone's IP without OK. Misappropriate = take secret wrongly.

Materially prejudiced: actually hurt in real way. Not small hurt.

Tender sole control: hand over full control. Other side drives.

Consent not unreasonably withheld: you can say no, but only with real reason.

Indirect / consequential damages: harm that flow from harm. Not direct hit. Example: broken software (direct) make you lose customer (consequential).

Incidental damages: side costs from problem.

Special damages: unusual losses tied to your situation.

Punitive / exemplary damages: extra money court add to punish, not to repay.

Theory of liability: legal path used to blame. Contract, negligence, etc. Cap block all paths.

Cumulative liability: all blame money added up, whole contract life.

Greater of A or B: pick bigger number. Floor is $100,000. Can be more if 12-month fees bigger.

WHY CARE
- Sued by outsider for other side's fault? They pay.
- Sued for your own fault? You pay, not them.
- Most money you owe: 12 months fees or $100K, bigger one. Except four no-cap cases.
- No lost-profit money, ever, except four no-cap cases.
- Get sued? Tell other side fast. Let them run defense. Help them.
